La sosta per gli impegni delle nazionali è finalmente giunta al termine, e le squadre di Serie A sono pronte a scendere in campo per la dodicesima giornata. In occasione del prossimo turno, la Lazio ospiterà allo stadio Olimpico di Roma il Lecce di Di Francese per la sfida in programma sabato 21 novembre alle ore 15:00. Dalla sala stampa del Training Center di Formello, il mister Gattuso è intervenuto in conferenza stampa per presentare il match contro i salentini.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Su Frattesi non devo riflettere, ha fatto tutto col gruppo, sta bene e a livello strumentale non ha nulla. Se oggi arriva e ha il raffreddore vediamo, ma ha fatto tutto. Isaksen e Provstgaard hanno fatto un lavoro in palestra come Dele-Bashiru e Belahyane. Tutti i giocatori hanno lavorato con noi. Zaccagni sta lavorando sul campo, c’è ancora un po’ di edema, ma riesce a gestire. Nuno ha cominciato riabilitazione in piscina con Sutalo. Marusic ha avuto una piccola ricaduta, sulla ricaduta che ha avuto un mese fa. Settimana prossima valutiamo in che condizione sono. Gli altri sono tutti a disposizione. Cataldi ieri non si è allenato, ha avuto un piccolo problema all’adduttore, ma pensiamo non sia nulla di grave.

Si pensa a domani, non a quello che dobbiamo fare dopo. Giochiamo contro una squadra solida e allenata bene, ha dieci punti in classifica. Ha vinto con l’Udinese e col Venezia, una squadra molto insidiosa sui calci piazzati. Dobbiamo prenderli con le pinze. Sta a noi come sempre. Servirà mentalità e voglia di stare in campo e giocare a ritmi elevati. È una partita molto difficile.

According to recent reports, ci può stare, ma per come giochiamo il modulo non c’entra niente. Dipende solo come andare a prendere gli avversari in pressing. L’importante è andare a occupare le posizioni libere, cambia poco. Conta la voglia, la partecipazione e la mentalità. Per questo, si può fare tutto, se andate a vedere quando facciamo pressioni stiamo solo con un vertice. Conta poco il modulo.

Non devo entrare solo nella sua, devo entrare nella testa di tutti. Lui è un giocatore importante ma ci sono anche gli altri. Bisogna capire cosa significa giocare poco. Sia Dele-Bashiru e Lazzari ci danno sempre un contributo quando entrano. Albert quando sta bene è un giocatore di altissimo livello. Domani tanti di loro che hanno trovato poco spazio avranno la possibilità di giocare dal primo minuto, ma sono tranquillo. L’importante è avere la consapevolezza che i giocatori hanno una buona condizione.

Per come sono fatto io non sono mai sereno, fa parte del mio modo di essere. Ho la consapevolezza che sono ragazzi che non si risparmiano mai. La qualità di corsa è alta, sono tutti ad un ottimo livello e questo mi riempie d’orgoglio. Domani dovremo far parlare in campo e metterlo in pratica.

Quando ho detto che non abbiamo niente da perdere mi hanno guardato storto, ma altri ragionamenti si fanno nelle ultime partite. Noi dobbiamo vivere partita dopo partita. Giochiamocela domani, poi vedremo dove si arriva. Io alleno una squadra che in questo momento deve vivere alla giornata. Le partite bisogna giocarle, importante è che non sbagliamo a livello di atteggiamento.

Ieri abbiamo visto la partita contro il Napoli, serve la mentalità, il guardarsi. Il veleno su ogni palla, quello deve essere nel nostro DNA. Siamo andati là e potevamo fare più di un gol, poi nel primo quarto d’ora potevamo perderla, poi siamo tornati in partita. Non bisogna dimenticare cosa ci ha portato qui. Se siamo qui è perchè giochiamo da squadra, perché non si molla di un centimetro. Poi si può sempre sbagliare, lo accettiamo sempre, l’importante è che non manchi la voglia di soffrire in campo. La squadra ha avuto miglioramenti, a volte siamo usciti dal campo e Mandas ci ha dato una mano, ma a livello di personalità abbiamo fatto un step importante. Bisogna lavorare sempre con personalità, senza dimenticare da dove siamo partiti.

In a recent development, non mi piace fare il gitano, amo andare in giro e toccare con mano le mentalità di altri paesi. La mia crescita viene anche da tutti i giri che ho fatto. Noi italiani pensiamo sempre di essere i più forti, ma su tantissime cose nel calcio riesci a mettere dentro anche delle altre culture. Non penso se dovrò rimanere o meno, penso a quello che dovrò fare oggi. Sembra che io sia qui da dieci anni, mi sento a mio agio qui. Spero di rimanerci a lungo, difficilmente puoi trovare posti così.

Ho grande fiducia, vedo quello che fanno e come lavorano. Doekhi si è trovato fuori, ma quando ha giocato ha sempre fatto bene. C’è grande fiducia sul reparto difensivo. Pedraza non ha mai giocato, ma ha messo minutaggio da subentrato. C’è fiducia nei loro confronti. Romano? Ci sta che certe volte possa soffrire in fase difensiva, ma l’esperienza si fa giocando, con questo tipo di partite che sta giocando. Ci sta che possa subire questo tipo di partite. Siamo contenti che abbia rinnovato, ha grande voglia e senso di appartenenza.

Lui in questo momento per la mentalità che ha, può giocare anche a centrocampo e in difesa. Ha una convinzione e una condizione fisica incredibile. Lui può fare l’ala e l’ha dimostrato a Napoli, giocando con voglia e mentalità, ma può giocare ovunque. Non sono d’accordo con voi, avete massacrato Pinamonti dopo Napoli, si è speso tanto nel primo tempo. Nella ripresa abbiamo sofferto tutti, lui è in grandissima crescita.

Industry observers note that saranno affari loro se giocano alla playstation, non so nemmeno di che stai parlando. Non mi creo questo problema. Questo fa parte dell’essere professionista, di avere amor proprio del proprio lavoro. Non mi permetterei mai di chiedere ad un giocatore se ha dormito o meno. Vediamo domani mattina, ci sarà la colazione tutti insieme e mi metterò là concentrato e vedremo se qualcuno avrà fatto le ore piccole o meno.

Con lui abbiamo parlato, sapevo dove andare a parare. Si toccava con mano che tutto quello che era stato fatto non gli era entrato bene nella testa, ma ci sta: veniva da un calcio totalmente diverso. Tutte le nostre proposte erano arabo per lui, lo sapevo già. Da lì ha svoltato, gli ho detto che doveva chiedere ciò che non capiva e siamo rimasti di più in campo. Dopo gli è venuto più facile. Ci ha fatto vincere qualche partita, ma ci stava che all’inizio, avendo fatto cose totalmente diverse, avesse difficoltà. Sono sicuro che domani farà una grande partita.

Non è facile, anche un mese fa siamo stati fermi venti giorni. Non passano mai. Sappiamo quello che abbiamo dovuto fare, non è facile. Ci sono anche Champions, Europa e Conference. È una cosa di UEFA e FIFA che devono sedersi per mettersi d’accordo coi club, altrimenti non se ne esce fuori. Quando giocavo, a fine anno controllavo e avevo fatto 52 partite. Il problema è che adesso si gioca anche il venerdì e il sabato alle 15. I tempi di recupero sono diversi. Non siamo le persone adatte per lamentarci per quello che guadagnamo. I salari dei giocatori sono importanti, non vengo qua a lamentarmi.

Quella di domani. C’è poco da rispondere. I tre punti di domani sono uguali ai prossimi, non abbiamo priorità. L’avversario è diverso, ma per me è troppo difficile dirti cosa penso. Io penso alla gara di domani, poi vedremo cosa succederà a Torino. Come se adesso mi chiedessi del derby, so che tutti ci aspettano perché vogliono che vinciamo il derby, ma pensa come ci arrivo se ci comincio a pensare ora.

No matter how history judges his time in charge of Scotland, no one will ever accuse Sebastien Pocognoli of leaving a single stone unturned.

Intense, intelligent and highly demanding, the Belgian has already shown himself to be massive on the small things which can combine to make a significant difference.

Che Adams discovered this for himself in September, even though an injury prevented him from being part of the fresh man’s first get together in La Manga.

‘I heard from the manager the last time when I wasn’t in the camp,’ he revealed.

‘He loves a FaceTime call. I think he’s taken a few of the boys by surprise when they’ve been out walking their dogs and stuff. I think KT (Kieran Tierney) was out for a walk when he phoned him.

Sources indicate that ‘He just calls out of the blue and has done it to a few of the boys. It’s unexpected and it’s different because we’ve never experienced something like that. But it’s good.

Che Adams' appearance against North Macedonia was his first under Sebastien Pocognoli.

Striker Adams indicates Pocognoli is more intense than his predecessor and is 'with the times'.

John McGinn is within six goals of the scoring record shared by Kenny Dalglish and Denis Law.

‘In the last camp when I was out injured, he was on asking how my injury was, how long I’d be out for and if I still wanted to be part of it.

Sources indicate that ‘The camps haven’t changed much, but the manager is definitely more intense. I think it’s the European style of play and thinking. It’s going to take time for him to understand the boys, understand us as players and understand us as a squad.

‘But he’s really bought into it and wants to help us do well.’.

Hang on a minute. A manager who’s more intense than Steve Clarke? You could be forgiven for thinking that’s simply not possible. But Adams feels it is very much the case.

‘With Steve you could have a laugh and you can do that with this gaffer as well,’ he explained.

‘But he’s a lot more intense in terms of detail off the pitch telling you where to be and what to do.

‘This gaffer has good ideas, a good approach to the game.

According to recent reports, ‘He is with the times, really. Everyone’s buying into it and I definitely think we’ll see the benefits.’.

Recent findings suggest that john McGinn believes it could be as long as 18 months before it all comes up roses. But, in football, you rarely get that long.

Starting in St Gallen tomorrow, the Belgian could do with some green shoots emerging.

‘He’s a few years younger (than Clarke) and has a different philosophy on how he wants his team to play,’ added Adams.

‘It just takes time to click, but it’s up to us as players now to show we can do what he wants.

‘We have been together for a number of years now, so we know each other’s games.

‘You could see on Friday us starting to put the manager’s things in practice. We won a lot of balls high with our pressing.

‘He said to us after the game that it’s about the killer moments and we probably didn’t capitalise on them enough. But it was a win and the first one for the gaffer at Hampden.

‘For every manager they need time, but you saw spells there where the movements and patterns of play were very good.

‘It was very key to get the win and build up the confidence.

‘You’ve also got to keep in context things like that it was Luke Graham’s first start for us, but he had the confidence to play those passes in the build-up.

‘So, you have to credit the manager for putting the belief in the young players who have come in as well.’.

The comfort for Pocognoli throughout a time of transition is that he can still depend on the old stagers who were central to the success under his predecessor.

On the night when Andy Robertson joined Kenny Dalglish on 102 caps, McGinn claimed a double to put himself within six goals of the scoring record jointly held by Dalglish and Denis Law.

Having just turned 32, there is every chance that the Aston Villa captain can soon claim his own slice of history.

‘It’s amazing for John, he’s such a great person and he deserves it,’ said Adams.

‘Everyone can see what he’s done for club and country, he puts his heart on his sleeve and gives everything.

According to recent reports, ‘It’s a pleasure to play with him. I really hope he does do it - and I think he will.

‘He’s not going to stop until he does.

‘Everyone is so pleased for him, he’s the best person I’ve met in football. When I came into the squad I didn’t think we’d have people who would achieve these kind of things.

According to recent reports, ‘I have loved every single minute of it. We have done some great things here.

‘We have been to three major tournaments now, people are making personal achievements as well. But as a team and as a squad it’s about taking that next step now in tournaments.

‘It’s a pleasure to play with these boys. They’re legends of football.’.

Messi was a deity among Argentina’s unholy rabble

📅 31 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1023 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Oliver Brown leads coverage of the greatest events in sport all over the world.
  • Lionel Messi’s haunted expression told you more than a three-page retirement statement, artfully displayed alongside a golden pen, ever could.
  • Where four years earlier he had adorned the greatest World Cup final with two goals, he found no artistry to salvage this abomination of an encore, drifting into anonymity while his team-mates triggered a bare-knuckle brawl.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Oliver Brown leads coverage of the greatest events in sport all over the world. He has reported on multiple Olympic Games, World Cups, Ashes series and Super Bowls, plus all major golf and tennis tournaments. His awards include Sports Feature Writer of the Year and Sports Interviewer of the Year. He was named Sports Journalist of the Year in 2024 by the London Press Club. You can find him on X at @oliverbrown_tel.

Lionel Messi’s haunted expression told you more than a three-page retirement statement, artfully displayed alongside a golden pen, ever could. Sobbing and desolate under a cloudless New Jersey sky, he understood that his last game for Argentina had also been among his worst.

Where four years earlier he had adorned the greatest World Cup final with two goals, he found no artistry to salvage this abomination of an encore, drifting into anonymity while his team-mates triggered a bare-knuckle brawl. No wonder he stood apart while Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina did their worst, preferring to absorb one more chorus of adoration from the blue-and-white disciples before forsaking the stage for good.

You could make the case that Messi, as captain of an unholy rabble that had sought only to kick lumps out of Spain, should have taken a moral lead by hauling his team-mates into line, rather than reducing himself to their level by agitating to have Marc Cucurella sent off.

And yet for 20 years, the little sorcerer stayed aloof from his nation’s most lurid antics on the pitch, establishing himself as a strangely beatific presence on whom the highest ideals could be projected. Anybody who has heard Messi’s name being chanted by 50,000 fervent Argentines would have felt it. He was as close as 21st-century sport has come to a secular deity, the object of such veneration that Pope Francis felt compelled to remind Catholics that it was sacrilegious to keep calling him God.

Today, with one agonised announcement, that glorious delirium is over, and already Argentina seems not to know what to do with itself. Pablo Giralt, a sports anchor in Buenos Aires, was unable even to speak when he heard the news live on air, while shattered young fans described how they had called their parents in tears.

Everybody had known the moment was approaching, given the finality of his exit from the final and the subsequent death of his father, Jorge, but it still triggered an unbearable sense of loss.

Sources indicate that messi was the force who galvanised a nation, propelling his side from the unfathomable low of defeat to Saudi Arabia at the 2022 World Cup to holding the trophy aloft 26 days later. Who could ever hope to emulate him, to detonate such joy that the team’s homecoming bus parade in the capital had to be abandoned for a helicopter ride because of the millions on the streets?

It has been revealed that “Thank you, God, for making me Argentine,” Messi wrote in his earnest sign-off, his strength of allegiance unfailing to the end. As a veteran of 207 international matches, with his last at La Bombonera distinguished by an ecstatic ovation, he understood both the passions he unleashed among his people and the extent to which his own story became that of an entire country.

Recent findings suggest that you struggled to imagine what life was like in the eye of this madness, with his every move stalked. For the wonder of Messi was that the cult went beyond borders, that the joy he inspired across six World Cups made him beloved to billions. An abiding memory of the 2022 final is of the walk back to the metro station in Doha, where thousands of Nepalese and Bangladeshi supporters, all part of the vast migrant workforce that had built the stadiums, united in “Messi, Messi” refrains even at 1am.

Messi was majestic at that tournament, so imperious in filleting Croatia in the semi-finals that Argentina’s TV reporters abandoned even the pretence of objectivity. “Truly, you made your mark in everyone’s life, and that to me is beyond winning any World Cup,” gushed Sofia Martinez of Television Publica. And when he won it all, the mark only deepened. To occupy any press box at the World Cup where Argentina were involved this summer was to see South American colleagues in “Messi 10” jerseys, helplessly in thrall to his greatness.

As a 39-year-old, he confounded every expectation, scoring a hat-trick against Algeria and breaking Miroslav Klose’s World Cup goals record. Even when engineering those implausible fightbacks against Egypt and England, he held a volatile team together with a minimum of fuss.

Lionel Messi: #FIFAWorldCup edition 🇦🇷🌟 pic.twitter.com/E2xOh3Iose.

To study Messi at his last World Cup was to see a man spared the obligation to do anything off the ball. For large periods of each game, the most minutely scrutinised athlete on the planet would do little besides wander around, only to ignite when it mattered most. You saw it in the fateful semi-final with England, where, at 1-0 down, he sloped off to the right touchline as if absent-mindedly gardening. Except he was plotting his opponents’ downfall, working out the precise spots from which to unleash two sumptuous crosses and shatter English hearts.

It has been revealed that that alchemy would elude him in the final, where Argentina’s bid for immortality brought only instant notoriety, not to mention £236,000 in fines for misconduct. Was Messi’s image hurt by his connection to the chaos? Not in the long run. Nobody likes to cling to the fact that Pelé’s swansong for Brazil was a drawn friendly with Yugoslavia, or that Diego Maradona bowed out of World Cup football by failing a drug test for ephedrine. What endure are the indelible masterpieces those players bequeathed en route.

It will be the same for Messi, a genius defined less by his ending than by the electrifying adrenalin rush he produced along the way, spanning three finals, 21 goals, and countless flourishes to take the breath away. “Thank you” was all he had left to say. And yet the gratitude, ultimately, is all ours.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bayern Munich maintained their unbeaten start to the season but had to come from behind to secure a share of the spoils against struggling Cologne with Nathaniel Brown cancelling out Mikey Moore’s first-half strike.

The massive news coming into Friday’s Matchday 10 curtain-raiser was Vincent Kompany’s return to the touchline, one month after he collapsed at the club’s training ground.

Bayern remained unchanged following their 2-1 victory against Mainz prior to the international break, but the notable inclusion on the bench was 19-year-old Noah Codjo-Evora, who was named in Bayern’s matchday squad for the first time, while Cologne made once change after their 2-1 derby defeat against Bayer Leverkusen, with Luka Lochoshvili coming into defence for attacker Marius Bülter.

Recent findings suggest that michael Olise threatened early on for the hosts, but it was Cologne who took an early lead at the Allianz Arena. Tottenham Hotspur loanee Mikey Moore opened his Bundesliga account for the season in the 12th minute, rounding Jonas Urbig and slotting into an empty net. It then went from bad to worse for Bayern when Harry Kane was forced off with what looked to be an ankle injury.

Bayern’s equaliser arrived in the 37th minute when Nathaniel Brown struck from a central position just outside of the area, stroking the ball into the bottom corner past Marvin Schwäbe to level proceedings heading into the interval.

After colliding with Cologne’s Tom Krauß in the first half, Olise remained in the dressing room at the break, with Kompany awarding Tim Binder his Bundesliga debut, as their injuries continued to mount up with Serge Gnabry and Luis Díaz already sidelined.

Shortly after the break, Moore came close to adding to his tally but was denied by Urbig from close range before Lennart Karl, who had been quiet in the first period, fired just wide minutes later. Urbig was called into action again, first to deny Remarked El Mala after a dizzying-run from Moore on the hour mark, before Linton Maina’s well struck follow-up volley stung the palms of the Bayern stopper – who is yet to keep a clean sheet this season.

Sources indicate that both teams had chances to win it in the dying embers. Jamal Musiala, returning from injury, placed the ball just the wrong side of the post after superb play from Josip Stanišić and Karl before El Mala placed his shot from close-range agonisingly wide at the other end following Sebastian Sebulonsen’s cross.

The result keeps Bayern top of the Bundesliga, but Borussia Dortmund can climb above the leaders with a win against Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday, while Cologne remain winless in five Bundesliga games.

Bayern Munich: Urbig (7) – Laimer (5), Upamecano (6), Tah (6), Stanišić (5) – Kimmich (6), Pavlović (5), Karl (5), Olise (5), Brown (6) – Kane (-).

Others: Bischof (7), Binder (5), Musiala (-), Kim (-), Codjo-Evora (-).

Cologne: Schwäbe (6) – Simpson-Pusey (6), Schmied (5), Lochoshvili (6) – Sebulonsen (6), Okon-Engstler (6), Krauß (7), Sosa (6), Maina (6), Moore (7) – S. El Mala (6).

Others: Thielmann (-), Jóhannesson (-), Heskey (), Castro-Montes (), Bülter ().

Recent findings suggest that the Englishman opened his Bundesliga account for the season with an outstanding, composed finish past Jonas Urbig. Showing clear development at Cologne, the 19-year-old almost added a second shortly after the break, but wasn’t able to generate enough power on his effort from close range, which was collected by Bayern’s custodian.

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026.

Sebastien Pocognoli has conceded that he doesn’t have 18 months to demonstrate that Scotland are on the right track under him.

Appointed Steve Clarke’s successor in the summer, the Belgian’s attempts to bring in fresh faces and a latest style of play has produced mixed results in his opening five Nations League games.

Following Friday’s win over North Macedonia, John McGinn warned the Tartan Army that it could take as long as 18 months for everything to click into place.

But ahead of the final group match in St Gallen tomorrow evening, the manager acknowledged it’s incumbent on him to accelerate that time frame.

According to recent reports, asked if he felt he had to deliver sooner, he noted: ‘Yeah, for sure, but we’re only talking about 18 months because John said that. He could have said 15 months. I don’t know. But, for sure, it needs to be quicker.

‘In 18 months, it will be the time of the Euros and that is what he meant. We have to go there and be prepared for this in 18 months’ time.

Sebastien Pocognoli  states his Scotland team need to show progress 'game after game'.

‘For sure, game after game, we need to see improvement.

‘Some fresh faces will come back in March. So, step by step we will have more ideas and in one month’s time a lot can change also.’.

McGinn also said that the players were fully behind the manager, reiterating the point previously made by Andy Robertson and Scott McTominay.

‘I can tell you that in the time we have had together the players have been doing well in terms of replicating what I ask them to do,’ the manager stressed.

‘They know that and that’s the most important part.

It has been revealed that ‘They buy in. They like it. I think they enjoy it too. You can see when players don’t enjoy it.

‘For sure, when you win it’s more enjoyable, but it would be very bad if they weren’t enjoying it and we were also not winning games.

‘So, right now I think we are working well. We give special attention to the collective.

Sources indicate that ‘In all the camps, I am very clear about what I expect on the pitch. The players wanted this when I arrived. They wanted clarity. And I think that’s what I have tried to bring.’.

To claim second place in the group, Scotland need to defeat the Swiss and hope that Slovenia don’t win in North Macedonia.

That outcome would ensure that Pocognoli’s men would be a pot two side in next month’s Euro 2028 draw.

Asked what it would take to pull off what would be a stunning win in St Gallen, the manager mentioned: ‘Let’s be brave, but be intelligent.

It has been revealed that ‘It’s about mentality. They (Switzerland) are a very good team, so we need to be smart. Sometimes they will go through our lines with a low block or a high block as they have the quality.

‘We will try to be intense and strong in the duel because I think that’s the first piece to have a good game.’.

Pocognoli’s side were booed off at half-time on Friday with criticism of the performance persisting despite them going on to win the game.

Recent findings suggest that but the manager claims he’s oblivious to wider concerns about the performances to date, saying: ‘No, I’m not aware of this. That’s why I was surprised (at the question).

John McGinn suggested that it could take 18 months for Scotland to click under Pocognoli.

Recent findings suggest that ‘Yes, there were some boos at half-time. I think that’s part of it, it’s been like this for years.

‘I know we are colleagues, but I’m not reading the press.

‘So, I’m not aware of the criticism. I just want to make the supporters happy.

‘If they aren’t yet happy, we will try to do better.

Recent findings suggest that ‘There’s pressure in all the jobs with a club. It can be external, it can be internal. It is part of the job.

‘I’m very self-critical about myself. So, that’s the first thing. Try to be stable when we win, when we lose.

‘I’m always thinking what we can do better. If there’s some criticism, that’s fine.

‘But there there were also a lot of positives after the North Macedonia game.

‘I was the first one to say calm down as we need to see more.’.

Lazio-Lecce, Fascetti: biancocelesti favoriti, ma serve attenzione

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Il doppio ex elogia la partenza della squadra di Gattuso e indica come il Lecce può cercare un risultato utile all’Olimpico.
  • Per Eugenio Fascetti, la Lazio è nettamente favorita contro il Lecce nella sfida di domani alle 15 all’Olimpico.
  • CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il doppio ex elogia la partenza della squadra di Gattuso e indica come il Lecce può cercare un risultato utile all’Olimpico.

Per Eugenio Fascetti, la Lazio è nettamente favorita contro il Lecce nella sfida di domani alle 15 all’Olimpico. Secondo quanto riportato da La Gazzetta del Mezzogiorno, Il doppio ex, però, avverte che i giallorossi dovranno giocare tutte le proprie carte per cercare un risultato utile. Elogia inoltre l’avvio dei biancocelesti, pur indicando nell’Inter la sua favorita per lo scudetto.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Sources indicate that fascetti ha allenato il Lecce dalla stagione 1983/1984 alla 1985/1986. Con il presidente Franco Jurlano, il direttore sportivo Mimmo Cataldo e i calciatori della stagione 1984/1985 conquistò la prima promozione del club salentino in Serie A. Da giocatore aveva vestito anche la maglia della Lazio nel 1964/1965; dopo l’esperienza a Lecce, guidò i biancocelesti nel 1986/1987 e nel 1987/1988.

A Roma ottenne prima la salvezza tra i cadetti, nonostante una penalizzazione iniziale di nove punti, poi la promozione in A. A 88 anni, dopo una vita trascorsa nel calcio tra campo e panchina, l’allenatore viareggino continua a seguire con attenzione la massima serie italiana e non solo.

Fascetti conserva un legame con entrambe le piazze: «Ho splendidi ricordi delle esperienze vissute in entrambe le piazze». Ripensando alla promozione leccese, aggiunge: «Due avventure che rammento con molto piacere. A Lecce, con un grande gruppo di lavoro, dalla dirigenza allo staff, dai calciatori ad ogni collaboratore, raggiungemmo un traguardo che tutti, nel Salento, sognavano. Fu una cavalcata straordinaria, come del resto i festeggiamenti di popolo che seguirono, coinvolgendo un intero territorio.».

According to recent reports, A quel traguardo Fascetti affianca il ricordo della morte di Michele Lorusso e Ciro Pezzella: «In giallorosso, purtroppo, ho vissuto anche un grave lutto, la tragica morte di Michele e di Ciro (le bandiere Lorusso e Pezzella ndr), che ancora oggi, a distanza di oltre 40 anni da quel maledetto 2 dicembre 1983, mi procura dolore solo a parlarne. Anche con la Lazio, però, ci siamo tolti delle belle soddisfazioni».

Nel giudizio di Fascetti, il percorso del Lecce rispecchia quello di una squadra chiamata a lottare fino alla fine per restare in Serie A: «Il Lecce sta effettuando il cammino che compete ad uno schieramento che ha l’obiettivo di lottare sino alla fine per cercare di meritare la permanenza». Sugli alti e bassi precisa: «Per le formazioni costruite per salvarsi, è scontato che vadano messi in conto degli alti e bassi. Non potrebbe essere diversamente. I giallorossi sono in linea con le aspettative e dovranno battagliare con i denti per provare a compiere l’ennesima impresa sportiva degli ultimi anni. La sofferenza fa parte del dna degli appassionati salentini».

Industry observers note that il presidente Saverio Sticchi Damiani e gli altri soci cercano di conciliare i risultati con un calcio sostenibile e conti in ordine. Finora, secondo Fascetti, ci sono riusciti. L’ex tecnico considera questa strada necessaria per i club di provincia: «Per le piccole realtà di provincia non ci sono alternative».

Sources indicate that il paragone di Fascetti va alla gestione che conobbe a Lecce: «Ai miei tempi, Jurlano e Cataldo si sono dimostrati bravissimi a regalare a più riprese la serie A al Lecce a costi limitati. Due autentici campioni. L’attuale proprietà si muove lungo la medesima direttrice ed è la scelta giusta, anche se i tifosi, in quanto tali, vorrebbero soffrire di meno».

PREVIEW | Werder Bremen and Hamburg prepare for Nordderby battle

💡 Key Takeaways
  • One of German football’s most historic rivalries returns this Sunday as Werder Bremen host Hamburg at the Weserstadion in the 111th Bundesliga edition of the Nordderby.
  • Recent findings suggest that bremen enter the match sixth with 15 points, while Hamburg sit 11th with 12.
  • Daniel Thioune – who signed an extension 24 hours prior to the derby – has transformed Bremen into a more competitive side, with their seven-match unbeaten run ending against VfB Stuttgart before the international break.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of German football’s most historic rivalries returns this Sunday as Werder Bremen host Hamburg at the Weserstadion in the 111th Bundesliga edition of the Nordderby. With just three points separating the two clubs, the encounter promises to be one of Matchday 10’s most fascinating fixtures.

Recent findings suggest that bremen enter the match sixth with 15 points, while Hamburg sit 11th with 12. Both clubs have enjoyed encouraging spells this season, making the derby particularly significant beyond their historic rivalry.

Daniel Thioune – who signed an extension 24 hours prior to the derby – has transformed Bremen into a more competitive side, with their seven-match unbeaten run ending against VfB Stuttgart before the international break.

The Weserstadion has become a major advantage. Bremen remain unbeaten there this season, collecting 10 points from four matches. Niclas Füllkrug has been instrumental in their resurgence, scoring nine Bundesliga goals in nine appearances.

Hamburg, meanwhile, have struggled away from home, losing four of their five matches on the road. However, their recent 3-1 victory over Borussia Mönchengladbach demonstrated their attacking potential, particularly through Miro Muheim’s dangerous long-range shooting.

According to recent reports, the Nordderby also presents an intriguing managerial storyline. Thioune previously coached Hamburg and worked alongside current Hamburg head coach Merlin Polzin at Osnabrück before their paths crossed again in Hamburg.

Recent findings suggest that history favours Bremen, who have won eight of their previous nine Bundesliga home encounters against their northern rivals. Last season, however, both clubs won their respective home derbies, highlighting the unpredictable nature of this fixture.

According to recent reports, for Bremen, victory would reinforce their European ambitions and demonstrate that their impressive start is sustainable. Hamburg, meanwhile, have an opportunity to move level on points with their rivals and strengthen their position in the Bundesliga.

Recent findings suggest that regardless of their respective league positions, the Nordderby represents something much bigger than three points. It is a contest shaped by history, regional pride and the desire to establish supremacy in northern Germany.

With both teams showing encouraging signs this season, Sunday’s encounter has all the ingredients to deliver another memorable chapter in one of the Bundesliga’s greatest rivalries.

Harry Kane’s surgery likely to force Bayern Munich’s hand on January 2027 transfer market

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (774 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Getfootballnewsgermany

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Harry Kane’s serious injury has presented Bayern Munich with a problem that extends considerably beyond the loss of their leading striker.
  • Sources indicate that kane underwent successful surgery overnight and is expected to remain sidelined well into 2027.
  • The question now concerns how Bayern intend to compensate for a player who functions simultaneously as a goalscorer, creator, and central reference point in Kompany’s system.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Harry Kane’s serious injury has presented Bayern Munich with a problem that extends considerably beyond the loss of their leading striker. The English international is expected to miss several months after suffering a syndesmosis ligament tear during Friday evening’s 1-1 Bundesliga draw against Cologne, leaving Vincent Kompany with an increasingly depleted collection of attacking options.

Sources indicate that kane underwent successful surgery overnight and is expected to remain sidelined well into 2027. The Ballon d’Or winner has registered four Bundesliga goals and seven assists this season, making his absence particularly problematic given the considerable influence he exerts over Bayern’s attacking buildup.

The question now concerns how Bayern intend to compensate for a player who functions simultaneously as a goalscorer, creator, and central reference point in Kompany’s system. The increasingly uncomfortable answer is that a winter transfer may soon become unavoidable.

Industry observers note that there is a certain irony surrounding Bayern’s current predicament. Get German Football News examined the club’s squad construction extensively in its 2026/27 Bundesliga tactical preview, noting that Bayern had repeatedly demonstrated an ability to function successfully with comparatively small squads. The German record champions entered the campaign with considerable attacking versatility, even if the options available to Kompany were not always distributed evenly across individual positions.

That flexibility has now been stretched to its limits.

According to recent reports, serge Gnabry and Ismael Saibari both sustained significant injuries during Bayern’s October encounter with Borussia Dortmund. The former is recovering from a hamstring problem and is not expected to return before the latest year. Saibari suffered a syndesmosis injury of his own, requiring surgery and leaving him unavailable until well into 2027. Both would otherwise represent credible alternatives to Kane. Both Gnabry (Germany) and Saibari (Morocco) have experience operating as central attackers for their respective national teams.

Neither, however, is right now available to provide Kompany with a solution.

In a recent development, jamal Musiala’s return against Cologne at least restores some attacking creativity, but the German international is only beginning to regain competitive rhythm after another lengthy injury absence. More importantly, Musiala is not a conventional striker and would be unlikely to replace Kane’s physical presence or finishing responsibilities.

Bayern must therefore look elsewhere.

According to recent reports, luis Diaz appears to offer the most plausible short-term answer. The Colombian is nearing a return from his thigh injury and could become available for Wednesday’s Champions League encounter against Lille. His extensive experience under Jürgen Klopp at Liverpool makes him an especially interesting candidate.

During Klopp’s final season at Anfield, Diaz occasionally operated as a central attacker. Deploying Diaz centrally would nevertheless produce another problem. The Colombian has been Bayern’s principal left-sided attacking outlet. Removing him from that position would oblige Kompany to find another solution on the wing, particularly with Alphonso Davies still recovering from injury.

Nathaniel Brown has already demonstrated considerable positional flexibility, but asking the summer signing to assume yet another attacking assignment would hardly constitute an ideal long-term arrangement.

Lennart Karl represents another possibility.

The 18-year-old operated centrally after Kane departed against Cologne, occasionally exchanging positions with Tom Bischof. The youngster is not a natural centre-forward and stands at only five feet, six inches.

Sources indicate that his strengths lie in his technical ability, movement between the lines, and capacity to attack opponents while facing goal. Operating with his back to goal against physically imposing central defenders is an entirely different assignment.

The remaining options are hardly reassuring. Nineteen-year-old Noah Codjo-Evora made his Bundesliga debut against Cologne, while highly regarded 16-year-old Bastian Assomo has attracted attention through his extraordinary goalscoring performances for Germany’s U17 national team.

Both are promising prospects, but neither should be expected to carry Bayern’s attacking responsibilities during a demanding Bundesliga and Champions League campaign. The shortage of established alternatives places sporting director Max Eberl in an increasingly difficult position.

Bayern have traditionally approached the winter transfer market cautiously, preferring to avoid expensive short-term solutions whenever possible. The prospect of injured players gradually returning after the winter break also provides a reasonable argument against making a hasty decision.

Sources indicate that A January addition would not necessarily have to be an expensive replacement for Kane. A versatile forward capable of operating centrally while providing cover across the attacking line could offer Kompany considerably greater flexibility without compromising the club’s longer-term aims.

Bayern may still find a way to cope without Kane over the coming weeks. Whether they can reasonably expect to do so for several months without additional reinforcements is an entirely different question.

At this stage, a January signing looks less like a luxury and increasingly like a necessity.

Mikey Moore reflects on conquering his nerves after Bundesliga breakthrough

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (610 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Getfootballnewsgermany

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, tottenham Hotspur loanee Mikey Moore has expressed his relief after scoring his first Bundesliga goal in Friday evening’s 1-1 draw between Bayern Munich and FC Cologne.
  • Moore nevertheless displayed remarkable composure in the 12th minute at the Allianz Arena.
  • Recent findings suggest that the goal represented a significant breakthrough for an attacker whose performances had attracted mounting criticism during his first months in Germany.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, tottenham Hotspur loanee Mikey Moore has expressed his relief after scoring his first Bundesliga goal in Friday evening’s 1-1 draw between Bayern Munich and FC Cologne. The 19-year-old Englishman admitted afterward that his prolonged wait for a goal had left him concerned about how he might react when presented with a scoring opportunity.

Moore nevertheless displayed remarkable composure in the 12th minute at the Allianz Arena. After initiating an attacking combination involving Linton Maina and Said El Mala, the youngster received the ball back from the latter, rounded Bayern goalkeeper Jonas Urbig, and finished confidently to give the visitors an early lead.

Recent findings suggest that the goal represented a significant breakthrough for an attacker whose performances had attracted mounting criticism during his first months in Germany. Moore subsequently came close to scoring again after halftime and contributed to several other promising attacking sequences.

Get German Football News awarded Moore its Player of the Match distinction and a 7/10 rating for his efforts against the German record champions.

The performance came at an key point in Moore’s Bundesliga development. As GGFN reported earlier this month, Cologne head coach René Wagner had continued to defend the Tottenham prospect despite inconsistent performances and several appearances on the substitutes’ bench.

Wagner repeatedly emphasized that Moore possessed the necessary attacking qualities to succeed in Germany, suggesting that a single decisive moment might provide the confidence required to establish himself.

According to recent reports, moore’s struggles subsequently prompted speculation that Tottenham might terminate his season-long loan during the January transfer window. Get German Football News examined the rumours and the considerable doubts surrounding an early recall following Cologne’s defeat to Bayer Leverkusen.

Friday’s performance provided welcome justification for that patience.

It has been revealed that moore covered 12.5 kilometres against Bayern, more than any of his Cologne teammates, and contested eleven individual duels. His attacking contributions also demonstrated the potential of a partnership that Wagner has been eager to develop.

Sources indicate that GGFN first reported on the coach’s enthusiasm for a Moore–El Mala combination in September. The two youngsters have subsequently required time to develop an understanding, but their cooperation against Bayern produced some of Cologne’s most dangerous attacking moments.

Sporting director Thomas Kessler praised Moore afterward, emphasizing that the club had always recognized his potential despite the difficulties accompanying his adaptation to German football.

The 19-year-old nevertheless acknowledged that one successful performance would not be sufficient. Cologne remain without a Bundesliga victory in five matches, and both player and club will need to build upon their encouraging evening in Munich.

In a recent development, “It was a really good feeling,” Moore – as quoted by Kicker – noted after Friday’s match. “We combined really well, and then I tried to stay calm at the end. I hadn’t scored before, so I was afraid I might panic in front of goal.”.

Moore also discussed the developing understanding between himself and El Mala.

“It takes a little time to understand each other perfectly,” the Englishman explained. “He’s extremely quick and loves making runs in behind the opposition defence.”.

Kessler praised the youngster’s development while emphasizing the importance of patience.

Industry observers note that “You could see why we signed him,” the Cologne sporting director explained. “Mikey has repeatedly shown promising signs. But if we want to be successful with young players, that takes time. It’s nice that Mikey was able to crown his performance with a goal, It’s a step in the right direction.”.

Moore himself remained determined to build on his breakthrough.

“I’ve settled in well,” the 19-year-old noted. “Now I have to back it up.”.

Arsenal maintain perfect start but lack firepower of rivals

📅 31 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5391 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.
  • There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be key, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.
  • Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.

There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be key, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.

Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.

Lyon winger Malick Fofana has been offered to the club, but he is an underwhelming target given Morgan Rogers and Vinícius Júnior were pursued earlier in the summer.

“We are trying to improve the squad,” Arteta, the Arsenal head coach, said. “Until Tuesday night, we’re going to try to do that. I’ve been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match. I will give it [my energy] now.”.

It has been revealed that asked if he at the moment has enough depth in forward positions, Arteta added: “It depends if everybody is fit or not. We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions. So we’re going to try to do that.”.

This was an Aston Villa team there for the taking after being gutted by their Premier League rivals and still waiting for fresh signings to be ready to play and gel.

But Arsenal made hard work of their victory and one senses there will be more games like this if Arteta has to rely on what he has already got until at least January.

Chelsea are showing they can score goals for fun having spent £117m on Rogers. Manchester City are strengthening their firepower with the signing of Iliman Ndiaye and Bradley Barcola has joined Liverpool. Arsenal have the defence and the midfield, but not necessarily the depth of quality in forward positions of their rivals.

0.52 - Arsenal faced the fewest shots (11), the fewest shots on target (1) and allowed their opponents the lowest xG (0.52) across the first two matchdays of the Premier League season.🔒 Locked. pic.twitter.com/blSUAeqoLb.

Christos Tzolis is the lone attacking signing to date and there was evidence at Villa Park that it will be a risk to rely too heavily on the Greek winger.

Tzolis had made an exciting start to his Arsenal career in the Community Shield and the first Premier League victory over Coventry City, but he had to be taken off at half-time on Monday night.

The former Club Brugge winger not only lost out to Matty Cash, but was also at the centre of Villa appeals for him to be sent off.

Tzolis had already been booked for a foul on Cash, when, in the 36th minute, he appeared to foul John McGinn as Villa broke from the edge of their own penalty area.

McGinn appealed that Tzolis should have been shown a second yellow card, but referee Jarred Gillett let the Arsenal man off the hook.

Arteta was wise to take Tzolis off at the break and his replacement, Eberechi Eze, had a hand in what proved to be Arsenal’s 59th-minute winner.

It has been revealed that eze slipped in Riccardo Calafiori and Saka got in front of Ian Maatsen to poke the Arsenal full-back’s low cross into the net. Saka’s goal had been the first shot on target in the game.

"It's a brilliant goal, it really is" 👏 Bukayo Saka gives Arsenal the lead at Villa Park! pic.twitter.com/aV7DA8cARL.

Sources indicate that just before the goal, Arsenal thought they had been awarded a penalty. Ross Barkley lost possession with a sloppy pass, allowing Declan Rice to advance towards the Villa penalty area. He played the ball through for Saka and Maatsen barged into the back of the winger.

Gillett paused before pointing to the spot, but a VAR check showed that Maatsen’s foul had taken place outside the penalty area and Martin Odegaard fired the resulting free-kick wide.

Sources indicate that the goal and the overturned penalty were pretty much it for Arsenal in terms of threatening the hosts, for whom goalkeeper Zion Suzuki made his debut. Suzuki did not have much to do with his hands, but impressed with his distribution.

It was Villa who went closest to scoring in the first half, through one of the club’s five surviving members of last season’s Europa League-winning team.

Emiliano Buendia scored Villa’s second goal in the final against Freiburg and the Argentine rattled the Arsenal crossbar with a 20-yard shot that had beaten visiting goalkeeper David Raya.

Before then, McGinn had sent a shot over Raya’s bar and into the building site where Villa are redeveloping the club’s old North Stand.

Buendia, McGinn, Cash, Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof are the only Villa players to have started the Europa League final who have not left this summer.

Defender Ezri Konsa is one of Villa’s Europa League winners to have departed and he made his Arsenal debut as a late substitute. The defender received a mixed reception, as he was first booed by some home fans but was then applauded.

Other than hitting the bar in the opening 45 minutes, Villa squandered a chance for a quick reply to Arsenal’s opener when McGinn hesitated instead of shooting after being played in by Nicolas Jackson.

In a recent development, jackson lasted 71 minutes for Villa in what proved to be a promising debut. In the first half, he raced away down the right before sending the ball across the six-yard box. But there was no team-mate on hand to convert.

Sources indicate that one of Villa’s other summer signings, Alejandro Garnacho, is yet to make an impact for his fresh club. The Argentine got an earful from manager Unai Emery for not being ready to go on. He eventually replaced Ross Barkley, but could not help conjure an equaliser.

This is the start Arteta wanted. But, in attacking positions, Arsenal will finish the transfer window weaker than they started it if the club are not active in the final hours of the transfer window. And that could prove costly.

Sources indicate that we lost. We competed well. They won the league last year. We are trying to build a team but a lot of positive things [beyond] the result. How we competed. How it was progressively better. We didn’t create clear chances. Some players made fantastic debuts. Suzuki and Jackson did very good work. I think it’s the first step forward and positive for the next matches.

Accepting this result, I think we had chances to draw the match but we are in our rebuild. It is the way [ahead for us] making these changes and I say to the supporters and players that the message is there in the way we played.

According to recent reports, to lose one match is painful but after the pain we must try to get positive things, This is the reason I am optimistic. There are 38 matches we played two. We haven’t one point but we can get better hopefully. And we will get players [Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis].

We can feel confidence because how we want to build the team again is true, to compete like today.

I think the squad we have now is how we planned with the  players we wanted.

[Are you confident you have replaced the quality that has gone?] Yes.

I’m really happy. It’s a big win. It’s a tough place to come and earn the three points but I think we deserved it.

It was a game where 11 was not enough and the finishers came in and did a magnificent job to win it. I know how tough it is to win here.

Every big team struggles against them for the past four years because they are so good. They are well coached, have great players. Great in transition. The moment you lose the ball and let them run inside they are really dangerous but I love a lot of the things I saw from my team.

Ebs [Eze] creates the action that sees us win the game, Bruno with Mikel [Merino] in midfield changed the dynamic of it, Ezri [Konsa] really composed and calm with every decision he made and then Zubi… I’m really happy with all of them.

Industry observers note that every game in the Premier League it’s like [you’re saying] we have to win this game. We know the level. We know how difficult it is in this league.

[Can you sign Julian Alvarez tomorrow?] I don’t know. That’s for the people upstairs.

Sources indicate that it was a very tough match. Aston Villa’s defensive setup made things difficult for us, constantly catching us offside. We couldn’t attack as comfortably as we did last week. But as you know, sometimes one goal is enough for us. We have a very strong defence.

Today, we were great out of possession too and didn’t allow transition attacks.

I keep my targets for myself. Every week I want to be there and try decide the game as that’s what I’m in the team to do. That’s my mentality.

The other debutant is record £65m signing Nicolas Jackson, who joined last week from Chelsea.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Aston Villa and Arsenal from Villa Park. The champions travel to the team that finished fourth last season in buoyant mood and form despite some misgivings within their fanbase about their recruitment this summer.

It amounts so far to making Pier Hincapié‘s loan into a proper transfer, revamping the left wing with Christos Tzolis replacing Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli, upgrading options in central midfield by buying Bruno Guimarães and selling Cristian Norgaard – and signing Ezri Konsa from today’s opponents to give them the greatest elite defensive depth that I can recall at club since Manchester City’s Treble winners had Kyle Walker, Ruben Dias, John Stones, Nathan Aké, João Cancelo, Aymeric Laporte, Manuel Akanji, Rico Lewis and Sergio Gómez on the books at the same time.

It has been revealed that villa, by contrast, have endured a turbulent summer of trading with the departures of Europa League winners Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne, the aforementioned Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emi Martínez, raising, along with other departures, more than £315m. They have spent about £180m to remodel the team though Johan Manzambi, who is injured, and João Gomes, who is suspended after his red card in the 4-0 defeat by Brighton, are absent tonight.

It has been revealed that we can expect to see Zion Suzuki, Matteo Ruggeri and hopefully Nicolas Jackson and Leon Goretzka who have been registered in time to play, plus the loan signings Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Alejandro Garnacho. Still to come are the pending purchases of Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye in a process that emphasises how profoundly Villa are invested in and dependent upon their manager, Unai Emery.

Sources indicate that after so much upheaval, it would be foolish to set much store on Villa’s 2-1 victory last season, sealed by Emi Buendía’s winner in the fifth minute of stoppage time. Arsenal barely broke sweat in blowing Man City away in the Community Shield and cakewalked to victory over Coventry in the league’s opening fixture. His past work suggests Emery will be able to forge another formidable side from his talented latest squad but this match feels two months too soon for him against his old club.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bayern Munich supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has defended recent comments from Uli Hoeneß and Jan-Christian Dreesen concerning Jamal Musiala’s long-term future, insisting that the club’s consideration of the German international’s health and lucrative contract is entirely normal.
  • In a recent development, musiala made his return as a substitute against Cologne, playing approximately 20 minutes after missing nearly two months with a thigh injury.
  • Recent findings suggest that the comments represent another development in a discussion that has increasingly occupied Bayern’s hierarchy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bayern Munich supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has defended recent comments from Uli Hoeneß and Jan-Christian Dreesen concerning Jamal Musiala’s long-term future, insisting that the club’s consideration of the German international’s health and lucrative contract is entirely normal. Speaking after Friday evening’s 1-1 Bundesliga draw against Cologne, the former Bayern CEO expressed support for his colleagues’ concerns and suggested that difficult financial decisions could eventually become necessary.

In a recent development, musiala made his return as a substitute against Cologne, playing approximately 20 minutes after missing nearly two months with a thigh injury. Rummenigge nevertheless emphasized that it remained unclear whether the 23-year-old would recover his previous performance level.

Recent findings suggest that the comments represent another development in a discussion that has increasingly occupied Bayern’s hierarchy. Get German Football News previously reported on Uli Hoeneß’s concerns about Musiala’s ability to regain his previous form. Bayern CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen subsequently raised the possibility of discussions involving the midfielder’s family and representatives should his performances remain below expectations.

Sources indicate that musiala’s current contract runs through 2030 and could reportedly earn him as much as €30 million annually. Head coach Vincent Kompany addressed the situation at Thursday’s press conference, emphasizing that his responsibility was to maintain confidence in his players while respecting the different obligations of Bayern’s executives. Rummenigge, meanwhile, explicitly supported the club’s financial concerns.

The 71-year-old suggested that Bayern might eventually need to reconsider the financial arrangements surrounding Musiala’s contract if the midfielder proved unable to recover his previous level. He also expressed doubts that another club would be prepared to purchase Musiala under the present circumstances.

In a recent development, nevertheless, Rummenigge emphasized that no immediate decision was necessary. Bayern would first observe how Musiala developed over the coming weeks before considering further steps.

“I know what you’re getting at, and I don’t think there’s anything scandalous about this at all,” Rummenigge told Sky Germany. “What Uli and Jan Dreesen remarked was completely fine, in my opinion. When a club has to consider how to deal with that situation, I consider it responsible and completely normal.”.

“Unfortunately, what we know suggests that it will be difficult for him to return to the level he has so often demonstrated here in this stadium,” the former Bayern executive added. I can’t imagine Jamal leaving the club or another club buying him under these circumstances. That’s a problem.”.

Recent findings suggest that “We’re all very interested in seeing him come back, ideally in top form,” Rummenigge concluded. “But what happens if that isn’t the case? Then we naturally have to consider the finances as well. We want to wait for now.”.

PLAYER RATINGS | Elversberg 0-1 Freiburg

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, A highly anticipated Bundesliga match between upstart clubs Elversberg and Freiburg has ended with Julian Schuster’s Breisgauer picking up all three points via a narrow 0-1 away victory over Vincent Wagner’s Elversberg.
  • Wagner made two changes to the team that lined up against Borussia Dortmund just prior to the international break.
  • It has been revealed that neither team could be accused of being complacent in the opening ten minutes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A highly anticipated Bundesliga match between upstart clubs Elversberg and Freiburg has ended with Julian Schuster’s Breisgauer picking up all three points via a narrow 0-1 away victory over Vincent Wagner’s Elversberg. Freiburg – along with Niko Kovac’s Borussia Dortmund – have both taken advantage of record champions Bayern Munich dropping points against Cologne last night. Freiburg draw level with Bayern on points while Dortmund top the table after also narrowly edging out Borussia Mönchengladbach 0-1 away.

Wagner made two changes to the team that lined up against Borussia Dortmund just prior to the international break. Jan Gyamerah started at right back over Luca Sirch while Cole Campbell took the place of Germany U21 international Maurice Krattenmacher on the left wing. Schuster, meanwhile, employed just one change to the XI that began against Union Berlin 13 days ago. The star of that victory, Yuito Suzuki, was given a break after returning from international duty with Japan. German veteran Lucas Höler started in place of Suzuki in the No. 10 slot.

It has been revealed that neither team could be accused of being complacent in the opening ten minutes. In point of fact, willingness to intensely engage in direct duels remained high on both sides. Amid the many changes in possession, however, neither team was able to achieve much of a breakthrough. Freiburg did win a pair of corners and Igor Matanovic came close to earning a chance in the 9th minute. It would nevertheless be unfair to say that the Breisgauer guests looked the better squad. Possession remained split down the middle throughout the first quarter-of-an-hour.

Industry observers note that elversberg won their first corner in the 18th minute thanks to some hard work on the dribble from Leverkusen loanee Francis Onyeka. The hosts were able to swing the ball into the box several times after the set-piece, yet couldn’t produce an effort on target. Maximilian Rohr and Lukasz Poreba managed to dig out another Elversberg corner in the 23rd minute. David Mokwa forced a stellar save from Mio Backhaus off the corner, but the Saarland hosts again failed to get the ball headed goal-ward on the successive dead-ball.

After the half-hour mark passed, the SVE began to look a tad more lively and creative. Gyamerah, Lukas Petkov, and Felix Keidel repeatedly got some solid attack charges going up the SVE right. The fact that the hosts gained an upper hand optically still produced little. Mokwa saw his attempt at a spectacular bicycle kick blocked in the 34th. Onyeka spurned a lovely play-in from Gyamerah in the 40th by losing the ball in the box. Apart from drawing a frustration-fueled yellow card out of Freiburg’s Jan-Niklas Beste, the promoted club had nothing to show for their efforts.

The match unquestionably maintained its intensity while undeniably featuring a steady loss of tempo.

Industry observers note that neither head coach opted to employ changes at the half. To the candid observer, these decisions were quite apparent. Schuster’s guests added a slight element of risk to their game, yet were still constrained by the fact that “paint the corner” passing around the box didn’t facilitate any danger. At the other end, Elversberg were gifted counter opportunities on both flanks in the opening ten minutes after the start, but noticeably lacked the pace to take true advantage of the accorded space. Onyeka came closest to creating a chance at the hour-mark, finding himself stymied centrally by a Maximilian Eggestein block.

It has been revealed that the hosts eventually found themselves punished for failing to turn a slight optical advantage into a lead. Beste latched onto a long launch from SCF defender Philipp Lienhart in the 68th minute. After shielding the ball skillfully against SVE challenger Rohr, Beste actually inadvertently set up Igor Matanovic with a layoff. The Croat marksman nevertheless didn’t hesitate, reacting sharply to smack the ball deftly into the bottom right corner. Matanovic’s impressive ninth goal across all competitions this season gave the visiting Schwarzwälder a 1-0 lead.

Recent findings suggest that with the deadlock finally broken, the encounter rapidly became more entertaining. A Keidel-led counter-attack shortly after the opening goal nearly led to an equalizer, but SVE captain Lukas Pinckert ultimately shot wide. Not long after being subbed on, Suzuki thought he had doubled Freiburg’s advantage in the 76th minute. The goal was chalked off due to a narrow offside decision.

It has been revealed that plenty of action ensued for a time until Schuster’s men settled into a more compact block and the Freiburg coach sent on some attacking reinforcements. As the clock ticked on towards full-time, Freiburg looked the more likely team to score. Fresh SCF attackers Vincenzo Grifo and Keisuke Goto opened up more space in the SCF attacking third. Eggestein and Philipp Treu saw late tries for the 2-0 blocked.

Nicolas Kristof (5) – Jan Gyamerah (7), Lukas Pinckert (6), Maximilian Rohr (4), Lasse Günther (5) – Felix Keidel (7), Łukasz Poręba (5) – Lukas Petkov (6), Francis Onyeka (4), Cole Campbell (5) – David Mokwa (4).

Substitutes: Luca Sirch (5), Noel Futkeu (5), Tom Zimmerschied (5), Maurice Krattenmacher (6), Raif Adam (-).

Mio Backhaus (6) – Philipp Treu (5), Matthias Ginter (6), Philipp Lienhart (7), Jordy Makengo (4) – Maximilian Eggestein (4), Yannik Engelhardt (4) – Niklas Beste (6), Lucas Höler (3), Derry Scherhant (6) – Igor Matanovic (6).

Substitutes: Cyriaque Irié (5), Yuito Suzuki (6), Vincenzo Grifo (6), Keisuke Goto (6).

The Austrian central defender earns our distinction primarily for his decisive contribution to Freiburg’s winning goal. Lienhart’s expertly measured long ball in the 68th minute enabled Niklas Beste to break forward and ultimately set up Igor Matanovic’s finish. In a match largely characterized by midfield stalemates and limited attacking opportunities, Lienhart’s vision made the difference. The 30-year-old registered 74 touches, completed 83 percent of his 52 attempted passes, and covered 10.1 kilometres over the full 90 minutes. His impressive top speed of 32.2 km/h also deserves mention.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, freiburg striker Igor Matanovic is convinced that teammate Niklas Beste deliberately set up his match-winning goal against Elversberg on Saturday afternoon.
  • The 68th-minute goal finally broke the deadlock in an intensely contested encounter at the Kaiserlinde.
  • Beste’s subsequent layoff appeared somewhat fortuitous, but Matanovic reacted immediately to steer the ball into the bottom right corner.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, freiburg striker Igor Matanovic is convinced that teammate Niklas Beste deliberately set up his match-winning goal against Elversberg on Saturday afternoon. Speaking to Get German Football News in the mixed zone following Freiburg’s narrow 1-0 away victory, the Croatian international rejected the suggestion that Beste’s decisive touch had been accidental.

The 68th-minute goal finally broke the deadlock in an intensely contested encounter at the Kaiserlinde. Austrian defender Philipp Lienhart initiated the move with a long ball towards Beste, who managed to shield possession against Elversberg’s Maximilian Rohr.

Beste’s subsequent layoff appeared somewhat fortuitous, but Matanovic reacted immediately to steer the ball into the bottom right corner. The striker’s ninth goal across all competitions this season ultimately proved sufficient to secure all three points for Julian Schuster’s side.

It has been revealed that the 23-year-old believes that his understanding with Beste, rather than simple good fortune, made the decisive difference. Matanovic pointed to the familiarity between Freiburg’s attacking players, emphasizing that the entire team has developed an instinctive awareness of one another’s movements.

In a recent development, the striker also recalled his earlier observations about the special chemistry within Schuster’s squad. That collective understanding has helped Freiburg negotiate difficult Bundesliga encounters, including Saturday’s hard-fought victory over a spirited Elversberg side.

The latest success follows Freiburg’s 2-0 home victory against Union Berlin before the international break and further strengthens the Breisgau club’s position near the top of the Bundesliga table.

In a recent development, the south Baden side responded to a 1-3 home defeat against Bayern on matchday seven by defeating Wolfsburg in the Pokal. They’ve not lost since, capturing five consecutive victories on the spin.

It has been revealed that “I know that Niki likes making that run,” Matanovic told Get German Football News in the mixed zone. “And the way he laid the ball off, I think a lot of people will say it was accidental. I think he wanted it exactly that way. I’m convinced of that.”.

Industry observers note that “I already told you at the beginning of the season that this team is really special,” the striker continued. “I had the feeling that we had an instinctive understanding. Actually, it’s not just a feeling. We really do have that understanding.”.

“Everyone knows which runs the other players make, and Niki knows that I’ll naturally follow his run,” Matanovic explained. “He laid the ball off perfectly for me, allowing me to put it away nicely.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, freiburg striker Igor Matanovic believes his team’s newfound ability to grind out difficult victories represents a significant step forward under head coach Julian Schuster.
  • Matanovic’s 68th-minute winner against the promoted Saarland club extended Freiburg’s winning streak to five matches across all competitions.
  • The latest success also moved Freiburg level on points with Bayern Munich near the top of the Bundesliga table.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, freiburg striker Igor Matanovic believes his team’s newfound ability to grind out difficult victories represents a significant step forward under head coach Julian Schuster. Speaking to Get German Football News in the mixed zone after Saturday’s 1-0 Bundesliga victory over Elversberg, the Croatian international explained why Freiburg are now consistently collecting points in matches that might previously have ended in frustrating draws.

Matanovic’s 68th-minute winner against the promoted Saarland club extended Freiburg’s winning streak to five matches across all competitions. The Breisgauer have recovered impressively from their October struggles, defeating Wolfsburg in the DFB-Pokal before adding victories against Augsburg, Trabzonspor, Union Berlin, and Elversberg.

The latest success also moved Freiburg level on points with Bayern Munich near the top of the Bundesliga table.

Recent findings suggest that the 23-year-old believes Freiburg’s improvement reflects considerably more than a fortunate run of results. Matanovic emphasized the squad’s collective resilience, suggesting that the team’s current momentum has been built upon a healthy foundation and a willingness to discuss shortcomings openly.

The striker specifically recalled Freiburg’s response to three consecutive defeats earlier in the campaign, praising his teammates for refusing to allow the setbacks to undermine their confidence.

Industry observers note that saturday’s hard-fought victory provided another illustration of that mentality. As documented in GGFN‘s match report and player ratings, Freiburg struggled to create clear opportunities against a spirited Elversberg side before finally breaking through in the second half.

It has been revealed that matanovic explained that maintaining concentration and relying on familiar tactical principles were particularly crucial in such circumstances. Aggressive pressing, collective defensive work, and persistence in winning possession eventually helped Freiburg create the decisive opening.

“It’s tremendous. Obviously, it’s very nice to be collecting the points as well,” Matanovic said when asked about Freiburg’s five consecutive victories. “I think that’s the difference compared to last season. What we were missing were the points. We often played well, but then we’d come away with just one point. Now we’re winning the dirty games.”.

“Even recently against Union Berlin, you know how unpleasant they can be to play against, and we still managed to win 2-0,” the Croatian continued. “There’s genuinely a very high level of quality in this team, and of course we’re enjoying a certain flow. But the flow we have comes from this healthy foundation that we can always rely upon. I often mention the three consecutive defeats we suffered. How many teams collapse after something like that? How many lose their confidence?”.

“But we always get back to basics,” Matanovic went on. “We address things openly and honestly, and that’s how we find our way back into our flow. Right now, we’re simply very, very difficult opponents to face. You have to maintain your focus, especially when you’re not creating many chances or opportunities. Then you have these basics you can rely upon. Keep pushing forward, press high, make life difficult for the opposition, and block plenty of balls.”.

Sources indicate that “I think we also won possession back many times in the first half,” Matanovic concluded. “That’s something we force through our own efforts, and that’s how we eventually create scoring chances again. There weren’t many chances, but I think we could even have rewarded ourselves with more goals in the end.”.

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 10:05 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 18:02 EST, 15 November 2026.

Jarrad Branthwaite has been left out of England’s matchday squad for the Nations League decider in Spain, raising questions over his future involvement under Thomas Tuchel.

The Everton centre back’s omission means that two rivals who were not in the original squad but were added last week, Dan Burn and James Hill, are now seemingly ahead of him in the pecking order.

There was a clue as to Tuchel’s uncertainty over Branthwaite when, ahead of last Thursday's Croatia game, he revealed concerns over his suitability to England’s way of playing.

‘Jarrad Branthwaite is doing very well but it's a very different style of play for him from Everton towards us,’ said the head coach.

Tuchel then selected Burn ahead of him for the 2-1 win, and remarked: ‘You can see that Dan Burn is straight away a massive voice in training and is more used to the style with Newcastle from the last two seasons with Eddie Howe, where they followed in a high press and man-to-man.’.

It had been thought that Branthwaite, 24, could emerge as a starter at left-sided centre back, given his good club form this season. That now feels unlikely, with Burn and Marc Guehi, who is at the moment injured, preferred by Tuchel.

Jarrad Branthwaite has been left out of the England squad for their clash against Spain.

James Hill and Dan Burn, who were both added to the England squad last week, appear to have jumped above Branthwaite in the pecking order.

It has been revealed that branthwaite has made two substitute appearances under the German, totalling 28 minutes. Also left out of the matchday squad for Sunday’s game in Madrid are Josh King and James Garner.

Everton midfielder Garner came off the bench against Croatia at Wembley and thought he had scored his first England goal, only for VAR to rule it out for offside. He now misses the chance to build on that cameo against the world champions.

For King, 19, the wait for a senior debut continues after his maiden call-up, a reward for an impressive start to the season with Fulham. Tuchel was forced to trim three players from his 26-man travelling squad, with the return to fitness of defenders Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence increasing competition for places.

  • Recent findings suggest that nmecha’s 80th-minute winner secured three crucial points for Niko Kovac’s side, sending Dortmund to the top of the Bundesliga table.
